items.title: Jane Monheit interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 20, 2010
items.q: But you know Mark O’Connor is on the record, John Pizzarelli is on the record, I mean these are huge names that people will recognize, and people who buy my records will recognize them, because I’ve been on tours with them and recorded with them

ctx.x: An awful lot. Because I’ve been arguing for them for years. But you know everybody seems to think that it’s going to be a big selling factor if you have a lot of star names on the record. My opinion on that differs. Because I know my audience and I pretty much

believe that with a few exceptions, you know getting a star rhythm section on the album there are going to be names that the people that buy these kind of vocal albums probably won’t recognize, and you’re going to end up with a band of brilliant, brilliant musicians who maybe aren’t that interested in playing with you and you end up getting a record that sounds very nice but isn’t as heartfelt, and you know I tour with my band constantly. I have for years. These guys are my brothers. And they are brilliant…
Well those people who go to your concert and buy the thing and want to get it autographed, that’s a plus for them too because they’re going to get what they just heard.
